chunks: And with this chain, from Umar ibn Sa'd, who said: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to me from al-A'mash from Ammar ibn Umayr al-Taymi, who said:

When the head of Ubaidullah ibn Ziyad (may Allah curse him) and the heads of his companions (upon whom is the anger of Allah) were brought, I arrived at them while the people were saying, 'It has come.' He said, 'So a snake came, weaving through the heads, until it entered the nostril of Ubaidullah ibn Ziyad (may Allah curse him). Then it came out and entered the other nostril.'

key_terms.الرُّءُوسِ: The heads, specifically referring to the severed heads brought to Kufa
key_terms.حَيَّةٌ: A snake, described as the miraculous entity entering the nostrils
key_terms.عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ: Ubaidullah ibn Ziyad, the governor of Kufa and key figure in the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (a.s.)
key_terms.مَنْخِرِ: Nostril, the specific anatomical part through which the snake entered

ai.seo_question: What miraculous sign occurred in the head of Ubaidullah ibn Ziyad after his death?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal* highlights the miraculous sign (karamah) of the severed head of Ubaidullah ibn Ziyad, where a snake entered and exited his nostrils, serving as a visible manifestation of divine retribution for his role in the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (a.s.). In Shia tradition, this event is often interpreted as the soul or spirit of the tyrant being tormented or expelled, confirming the spiritual reality of the afterlife even before physical death. The presence of the people witnessing this phenomenon underscores the public validation of the Ahl al-Bayt’s cause and the immediate divine justice meted out to their enemies.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 9. And from the previous chain from Umar b. Sa’d who said it was narrated to me by Abu Muawiyah from al-’Amash from Ammar b. ’Umayr al-Taymi who said:

Ammar bin Umair Tamimi narrates that when the heads of the cursed Ubaidullah bin Ziyad and his companions were brought, people were saying that a snake was wrapped around his head and it went inside the head of Ubaidullah through a nostril. Then it came out and, entered the second nostril.
